still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US. Generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market, and exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels, and the 503B compounding exclusion finalised in 2026 still stands.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance still lets wellness programmes tie up to a 30% premium differential to fill-verified adherence or BMI outcomes, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still in force.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 25.5% ever-used minus 18.6% current leaves 6.9% of adults who have used the drugs and are off now. 44% of ever-users have cycled, which is 11.2 points: about 9.6 points are current users on at least their second course (52% of current users), and about 1.6 points have cycled before and are off again. That is consistent with roughly one-third persistence at one year and 36–47% restarting within a year, compounded over more cycles. 18.6% of ~268M adults is ~50M current users. Age-weighted check: 0.20×10 + 0.33×19 + 0.24×30 + 0.23×14 ≈ 18.7. Payer mix of the 50M: commercial ~28% (~14M, flat in headcount while employer weight coverage fell, held up by diabetes, cardiac and new AUD codes; ~4.5M of these are in adherence-verified tracks), Medicare ~18% (~9M: diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk and, since Feb 2030, AUD codes), Medicaid ~11% (~5.5M, up because the AUD indication falls under mandatory Medicaid drug coverage), federal free provision (Community Metabolic Access Program) ~3% (~1.5M), legitimate cash ~31% (~15.5M), gray-market telehealth/imported/compounded ~9% (~4.5M, up from ~3M). The bottom third rose 11% → 14% mostly through free provision and Medicaid AUD coverage, not employers. Never-users remain a population: ~23% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated among the near-poor above the free-provision income line, small-employer workers whose plans dropped coverage, and rural adults far from FQHCs. Under-18 use (1.1%) is concentrated in 12–17-year-olds in upper-income households; about 1 in 4 adolescents with severe obesity in the top income third is on a drug, versus about 1 in 14 in the bottom third.

access.public_coverage: Medicare Part D still cannot cover weight loss alone, but covers incretins under diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, MASH, dementia-risk (tirzepatide, PA) and, since Feb 2030, alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide) codes, at the negotiated semaglutide maximum fair price (~$274/month). AUD increment: ~1.4M Medicare users × ~$274 × 12 ≈ $4.6B/year run-rate by late 2030. Medicaid must cover the AUD indication under the drug rebate statute, and every state now does, mostly behind PA requiring an AUDIT score and a counselling referral. Weight-only Medicaid coverage is in 8 states (9 in 2028, minus 2 dropouts, plus 1 new state). Federal free provision: HRSA's Community Metabolic Access Program (launched Oct 2029) supplies oral semaglutide free at FQHCs to uninsured or non-covered adults ≤200% FPL with BMI ≥35, type 2 diabetes or AUD. It buys at a negotiated $149/month. Arithmetic: ~1.5M enrolled × $149 × 12 ≈ $2.7B annualised. The FY2030 appropriation was $2.9B, and actual FY2030 outlays were ~$1.9B because of ramp-up. Continuation requires a 6-month clinic visit.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian and Chinese generic semaglutide costs $5–35/month in 170+ countries, and Canadian generics are CAD 60–95. Generic liraglutide is everywhere. Indian firms have begun exporting 'research' tirzepatide and retatrutide analogues into unregulated channels, ahead of any patent expiry.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline: the Jan 2029 TrumpRx round cut maintenance orals to $199–249 (Wegovy pill $199, Foundayo $149–249) and branded injectables to $249–349. Retatrutide (approved Mar 2029) lists ~$1,290 and sells for $499 cash, and the tirzepatide+bimagrumab co-pack (Sep 2030) is cash ~$899, which is why both are pulled into gray channels. Employers covering weight management fell 44% → 34% (Business Group on Health, 2030), and another 12% cover only through monitored metabolic tracks. Orals are ~58% of new starts and ~46% of all users. The gray market regrew through three routes: 503A 'patient-specific' compounding of tirzepatide 'with B12' and of 'muscle-sparing stacks', 'research-use-only' peptide sellers paired with telehealth prescribers, and mail-order Indian vials. About 4.5M users, many of them on next-generation molecules priced out of the legal market.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2029)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
Incretin + activin-receptor antibody co-pack (tirzepatide weekly + bimagrumab monthly subcutaneous, approved Sep 2030)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial ongoing)
alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide 25 mg, Feb 2030; ASAM and APA guideline endorsement Nov 2029 ahead of approval)
preservation of lean mass during weight reduction in adults with obesity aged 50+ or at risk of sarcopenia (tirzepatide + bimagrumab co-pack, Sep 2030)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction below AUD thresholds ('moderation dosing'), now EAP-standard and only nominally off-label
dementia-prevention use by people without CVD, cash-paid on orals
compounded 'muscle-sparing stacks' (incretin plus unapproved myostatin or activin peptides) sold via telehealth
nicotine and gambling reduction, observational support only
drugs.pipeline_note: Retatrutide was approved in Mar 2029 on its extended timeline, with dysesthesia and discontinuation language in the label. It is the efficacy leader (~27% in pivotal data), but cash pricing keeps uptake under 1M legal users. Oral semaglutide for AUD was filed in Feb 2029 after phase 3 and approved after standard review in Feb 2030, 12 months later. The muscle-preserving driver arrived as a co-pack rather than a new molecule. Bimagrumab's phase 3 portion read out in early 2029, Lilly filed the tirzepatide+bimagrumab co-pack in May 2029, and the FDA approved it in Sep 2030 after a 3-month extension. The label claims lean-mass preservation on DXA, with no fracture or function outcome claim. Marketing ('lose the fat, keep yourself') sells the 'skinny-frail' problem as solved, though the evidence shows only that it is attenuated on imaging. Survodutide received a Complete Response Letter in Jul 2029 on manufacturing, and its resubmission is pending, so a 2031 decision is likely. Amycretin was filed Jun 2029, with a decision no earlier than mid-2030, then extended to 2031. MariTide (monthly) filed in Oct 2030 and is not on the market. No oral yet matches tirzepatide. Global incretin market ~$135B (2029); US net prices are falling 5–8% a year through negotiated channels, offset by volume.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Retatrutide's GI profile is in line with tirzepatide at matched weight loss.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged in magnitude.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL settlements largely concluded in 2029.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 2028 Medicare hip-fracture signal (HR ~1.3, 65+, >2 years of use) was replicated in a 2029 VA cohort. Bimagrumab co-pack trials show lean-mass loss cut by about half on DXA, with no fracture data. Risk remains concentrated in older women, low-protein users and repeated cyclers, and increasingly in gray-market users with no monitoring.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Jul 2028 class warning stands. The CMS DXA code is used heavily. The co-pack label carries the class bone warning unchanged, and FDA required a fracture-outcome postmarketing study.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflicting; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the AUD programme.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The AUD phase 3 included an anhedonia scale and found meaningful rises in ~6% on drug versus ~3% on placebo, consistent with the 2027 cohort. Dose-related and partly reversible. No new kind of signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA postmarketing observational study ongoing. The AUD label mentions 'decreased interest or pleasure' among adverse reactions; there is no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Retatrutide discontinuers regain faster in absolute terms.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy framing and adherence monitoring.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More B12, iron and vitamin D case series, concentrated among low-dose and gray-market users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; FQHC programme protocol includes baseline labs. No label change.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; adolescents on decades-long therapy; repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up exists. Adolescent bone postmarketing data are not yet reported.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone-density PMR pending; no new action.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product rose from ~6,400 (mid-2028) to ~11,000 (mid-2030), in line with the larger gray-market population; no new kind of harm. Poison-centre mg/unit calls are still rising. Unlabelled 'stack' vials are a growing share of reports.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Sep 2029 FDA/DOJ action against peptide telehealth networks; warning letters to 503A pharmacies; import alert stands. Personal importation remains porous.

food_and_beverage.state: About a third of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~7–9% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~7%, and dollar sales are roughly flat through price and premium protein lines. The split now runs by class: high-protein, high-price 'performance' grocery grows in upper-income ZIP codes, while discount chains (Dollar General, Aldi) hold volume in conventional snacks. Volume pressure has moved from middle-income suburbs to upper-middle ones.

alcohol.state: The AUD approval turned EAP referral into prescription. US spirits volumes are down ~11% from 2025 and beer ~7%. Heavy-drinker loss is concentrated in insured working-age men. Brown-Forman closed another Kentucky bottling line in 2030. Non-alcoholic and 'occasion' premium lines grow but do not replace volume. Bars in mid-sized Midwestern cities (Columbus, Indianapolis) report weeknight closures.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat, checks pressured. Small-plate, protein-forward menus are permanent. Fine dining has re-priced around tasting portions. Buffets keep closing. Late-night alcohol revenue in casual dining is down sharply.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Upper-income buyers drive 'athletic tailoring', cut for shoulders and arms that read as preserved muscle. Value chains stock wide size runs and stretch fabrics for a cycling, regaining customer base. Rental and resale take more of the size churn.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. DXA and body-composition chains (now in most metros) market scans as status as well as safety. The bimagrumab co-pack has prompted some premium clubs to sell 'protocol memberships'. Budget gyms grow more slowly.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is down to 34%, with 12% more through monitored tracks only. Pharmacy trend is ~+7%, slowing as net prices decline. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, cardiac, dementia and AUD codes, and AUD codes have become a back door that PBMs police with AUDIT-score PA. Premium differentials tied to adherence are common in large self-insured firms outside Illinois and California.

pharma.state: Lilly and Novo dominate. US net prices are falling through TrumpRx, Medicare negotiation and the HRSA purchase contract, while volume grows. Retatrutide and the co-pack are premium cash and commercial products. Brand-protection and litigation against peptide telehealth is a growing cost line. Ex-US is a generic volume market.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body composition, not weight, is now the readable signal. Lean with visible shoulder and arm mass reads as top-tier: branded drug, co-pack or retatrutide, DXA, trainer. Lean and soft reads as middle: a covered or cash oral. Heavier or visibly regained reads as uninsured, cycled off, or 'on vials'.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Thinness alone stopped signalling wealth once free provision and Medicaid AUD coverage reached the bottom third. Muscle took its place. In Plano, Buckhead and Bethesda, women aged 55–70 compare DXA lean-mass percentiles at book clubs. Below them, FQHC patients on the free Wegovy pill are thinner than they were and still read as poor, because they lack the preserved-muscle look. Gray-market retatrutide lets young working-class men buy the top-tier look without its monitoring.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter. Church fasting networks (the Tulsa 'Bread Alone' network claims ~650 congregations) have added drug-free Lenten and Ramadan fasts as explicit class critique. Protein-heavy 'plating' is an upper-income hosting norm. Holiday tables still accommodate guests who are not hungry.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps show 'on/off' badges and, among premium users, 'DXA verified'. Desire mismatch remains a staple presenting problem. Sobriety-by-prescription changes dating scripts, and 'drinks' first dates are giving way to walks and gyms in insured professional circles.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Institutions treat appetite, including thirst for alcohol, as noise to manage. The refusal coalition (fat-acceptance groups, Unmuted, church fasters, MAHA-aligned legislators) now speaks the language of class: appetite as one of the few things the poor were never charged for.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Measured anhedonia in ~6–7% of users versus ~3% of controls, replicated in the AUD trial. With ~50M users, that is roughly 1.5–2M people above the background rate. Many more report a milder 'evenness' that employers count as a benefit.
interior_life.framing: Employers call it 'steadiness' and, since the AUD approval, 'recovery support'. Clinicians call it a side effect. Unmuted calls it sedation. Most users don't name it at all.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 4.5M employees are in adherence-verified tracks. Logistics, call-centre and state employers have added the AUD indication to EAP pathways, so a drinking-related disciplinary note now commonly carries a referral to a prescriber. Adherence data stay out of personnel files on paper, but managers in tracked firms know who is in the programme. In Aug 2029 the EEOC found cause on one of the two ADA charges, against an Indiana logistics firm whose differential penalised a worker who stopped because of vomiting; the case is in conciliation. DOT ruled in 2029 that incretin use is not disqualifying for CDL holders.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle per identifiable user keeps falling. Unmuted's 'off nights' have spread to Chicago and Oakland. The 'flat' fiction wave has a counter-genre about hunger and the poor. Gym culture is the dominant leisure aesthetic among the insured.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples sync doses or schedule drug holidays. Partners of former heavy drinkers describe relief and estrangement at once. Therapists report spouses asking whether the person they married was the drinker or the drug-free self.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Coalition politics more than mood. California passed AB 1182 (2029), capping adherence-conditioned differentials at 10% and banning BMI-outcome conditions. Bills are pending in New York and Colorado. The free-provision programme has scrambled the alliances: MAHA-aligned legislators attack it as pharma welfare, while some fat-acceptance and labour groups defend it as the only access the poor have. No evidence of a 'sedated electorate'.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-speed on approvals: retatrutide, the AUD indication and the co-pack were all approved inside the window. FDA and DOJ have taken a harder line on telehealth peptide networks since Sep 2029, but 503A loopholes and personal importation remain porous.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Direct subsidy: HRSA's Community Metabolic Access Program (Oct 2029) gives free oral semaglutide at FQHCs, ~1.5M enrolled, ~$2.7B annualised at $149/month. HHS framed it explicitly as displacing the gray market and reducing alcohol harm. TrumpRx cash prices continue, and the Medicare MFP applies to semaglutide.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: PBM fill data and app-linked dose logs feed wellness vendors. Six state employee plans cover weight-loss incretins only through monitored tracks. Three Medicaid programmes tie continued weight coverage to adherence and BMI. The FQHC programme requires a 6-month visit but no BMI target, after HRSA dropped the target under pressure. Medicaid AUD prior authorisation requires an AUDIT score.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE still restricts weight-only coverage, but covers the AUD indication. The Army's supervised oral pilot for near-standard recruits expanded to the Marines in 2030. DOT allows CDL holders on incretins.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply most of the world's semaglutide and now ship unapproved tirzepatide and retatrutide analogues. US–India trade talks added peptide export controls in 2030, and they are weakly enforced. Manufacturers trade US price cuts for tariff treatment.

events.event: New TrumpRx price round cuts maintenance Wegovy pill to $199 and branded injectables to $249–349; $149 starting dose unchanged
Business Group on Health survey: employers covering GLP-1s for weight loss fall to 34%, a further 12% only through adherence-monitored tracks

FDA and DOJ move against telehealth networks selling compounded tirzepatide, 'research' retatrutide and unapproved 'muscle-sparing stacks'; regulators estimate 4M+ Americans buy outside legal channels
HHS launches free oral semaglutide at community health centres for low-income uninsured adults with severe obesity, diabetes or alcohol use disorder, at a negotiated $149 a month
FDA approves oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder; Medicaid coverage becomes mandatory and Medicare Part D opens a new non-weight route
FDA approves Lilly's tirzepatide-bimagrumab co-pack for weight loss with lean-mass preservation in adults 50+; label carries no fracture claim

open_tensions: The co-pack and DXA culture sell muscle as solved and as status, while fracture outcomes are unproven and the cheapest users (FQHC orals, gray-market vials) get neither the adjunct nor the scans. The bone gap now runs along class lines.

The AUD indication turned workplace drinking discipline into a prescription pathway, as the AUD trial confirms blunting in a minority. The EEOC's cause finding and California's 10% cap test whether 'steadiness' and 'recovery support' can be conditions of employment and insurance.

Free federal provision reached the poor just as employers retreated from the middle. The near-poor above 200% FPL with small-employer plans are now the least-served group, and they are the gray market's growth base, including for retatrutide.

The HRSA programme's ~$2.7B run-rate depends on annual appropriations and a $149 contract price. MAHA legislators want it gone, and Medicare's AUD and dementia routes are growing faster than any CBO score anticipated.

prose.headline: Thin Is Free Now. Muscle Costs $899. Inside America's new body economy, where the clinic, the boss and the mail all sell steadiness
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030 almost one American adult in five is taking an incretin drug, about fifty million people, and a quarter of adults have tried one. The drugs no longer mark anyone out. What a body says now depends on what it is made of.

Prices have come down slowly. In January 2029 the government's cash channel cut the maintenance dose of the Wegovy pill to $199. Starting doses stayed at $149, and branded injectables now sell for $249 to $349. The $1,349 list price is still printed on boxes. No American generic exists, and none will before 2031. Everywhere else in the world, an Indian vial costs less than a sandwich.

Employers kept retreating. Only about a third still pay for the drugs for weight loss alone. Another one in eight pays only through metabolic tracks that check pharmacy fills and app logs and tie up to thirty percent of the premium to staying on the drug. The coverage that remains runs through diagnosis codes: diabetes, heart, kidney, dementia risk, and since February, alcohol. That month the FDA approved oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder. Medicaid now has to cover it and Medicare can, because a drinking problem is not a weight problem in the statute's eyes. Employee assistance programmes noticed first. In logistics and call-centre firms, a write-up for drinking now often comes with a referral to a prescriber. HR decks call the result recovery support, and they still call the mood steadiness. The alcohol trial measured lost pleasure in about six percent of patients, twice the placebo rate, and the label mentions it in small type.

The poorest Americans got something new as well. Since October 2029, community health centres have handed out the Wegovy pill free to low-income uninsured adults with severe obesity, diabetes or alcohol use disorder. Washington buys it at $149 a month for about a million and a half people. HHS sold the programme as a way to drain the mail-order market, and MAHA-aligned legislators attack it as pharma welfare. The people most left out are the ones just above the income line, working for small firms whose plans dropped coverage.

The gray market grew back to meet them. It runs through telehealth sites and compounding pharmacies and moves faster than the agencies. Retatrutide, approved in March 2029 and the strongest drug on the market, sells legally for $499 cash and for a fraction of that as 'research peptide'. Young men from gyms and job sites inject it from unlabelled vials. Regulators think more than four million Americans buy outside legal channels. Adverse-event reports have roughly doubled since 2028, and contaminated lots no longer surprise anyone.

In September the FDA approved Lilly's co-pack of tirzepatide and bimagrumab, which roughly halves the muscle loss that comes with dieting by drug. The advertising says the skinny-frail problem is solved. The label says lean mass looks better on a scan. It says nothing about broken hips, and the class bone warning is unchanged.

Muscle is what money buys now. In Plano and Buckhead, women in their sixties compare DXA percentiles and buy jackets cut for their shoulders. FQHC patients are thinner than they were and still look poor. Spirits volumes are down a tenth from 2025, and weeknight bars in Columbus close at ten. California capped adherence premiums at ten percent. The EEOC found cause against an Indiana warehouse that penalised a worker for vomiting. Tulsa's fasting churches now preach against the drug as a class matter. From the outside, the country looks soberer, thinner and calmer. Most of that is true.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tanya Whitlock takes her pill at 5:40 with four ounces of water, standing at the sink in her Dayton kitchen, and then has to wait half an hour before coffee. The bottle has a white HRSA sticker and the FQHC's phone number. She pays nothing. Her six-month visit is Thursday. She has written that on the fridge, under her grandson's drawing of a truck.

By eight she is at Mr. Kessler's in Oakwood. He is eighty-one, a retired engineer, on the dementia shot through Part D. His daughter has a DXA printout taped inside a cabinet with his lean mass circled in green. Tanya makes him eggs and cottage cheese because the printout says protein. He eats four bites and says, pleasantly, that he isn't hungry. He is never hungry anymore. He hasn't asked about the Bengals since spring.

At lunch she eats half a turkey sandwich in her car and saves the other half, the way she does now.

Her son Darnell texts from the warehouse at two: *boss says the plan thing is mandatory for leads.* An hour later: *or I pay more.* He already buys something called reta from a site with a tiger logo, ninety dollars for a vial. He keeps it in the butter compartment. She doesn't ask what it is. His arms look like the men's in the ads.

The agency's next client, Mrs. Ochoa, still has a ripe banana on the counter and sings along to the radio. Tanya catches herself watching her.

On the drive home she passes the bar on Wayne Avenue. The neon is off. It's Tuesday.
